clue.text: Items of jewellery finish inside underwear

indicators.note: inside tells us the word for finish sits within the word for underwear

parts.note: pants are underwear
the finish of something is its end

explanation.surface: A slightly risqué image of jewellery tucked away in someone's underclothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanging ornaments worn on a chain round the neck are a kind of jewellery.

clue.text: They supply drink — buffoon delivers

parts.note: Mr Punch, the puppet show clown, is a buffoon
in cricket a bowler delivers the ball, i.e. bowls

explanation.surface: A clown serving drinks at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: Punch is the slapstick puppet of British Punch and Judy shows; in cricket, bowling a ball is called delivering it.
explanation.definitionFit: Large bowls from which a mixed party drink is ladled out supply that drink to guests.

clue.text: Son should stay off the cocaine today

indicators.note: staying off means the letter for son is removed from the word for cocaine

parts.note: snow is slang for cocaine

explanation.surface: Advice that a young man should give up drugs, starting immediately.
explanation.definitionFit: Today and the present moment are synonyms, as in 'people live longer these days'.

clue.text: Side beginning to cheer something hovering above?

parts.note: side means pretentious manner, as do airs ('putting on side', 'giving oneself airs')
the opening of a cheer is 'Hip, hip, hurrah', so hip begins the cheer

explanation.surface: A team, or one side of a crowd, starting a cheer as something floats overhead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Side' looks like a team or edge but means affected superiority, an old British sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirigible balloon is a craft that floats in the sky overhead, hence the question mark for this loose description.

clue.text: Those people on river, some turning up for play

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: them stands for those people
the Ouse is a river in England

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word for some is read upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: part means some, as in 'part of the cake'

explanation.surface: A group of people on a river, some of them rolling up for a theatre performance.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is an English river (one runs through York). 'turning up' reverses PART to TRAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha Christie's long-running London stage thriller is a well-known example of a play.

clue.text: Name engraved in broken strip of wood

indicators.note: engraved in means the letter for name is cut into the word for broken

parts.note: split means broken, cracked apart

explanation.surface: A name carved into a cracked piece of timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigid support strapped to a broken limb was traditionally a thin piece of timber.

clue.text: Commended as pressure increased

parts.note: raised means increased, as with prices

explanation.surface: Someone praised as the pressure on them grew.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak well of someone is to laud them; commended and lauded are synonyms.

clue.text: So, prose line converted into poem

indicators.note: converted into tells us the letters of so, prose and line are changed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A remark that a piece of prose has been turned into verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton's pensive lyric, companion to L'Allegro, is a famous English poem.

clue.text: Sailor comes to port finally for loose woman

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor

indicators.note: finally picks out the closing letter of the word port

explanation.surface: A seaman coming ashore and finding a woman of easy virtue.
explanation.definitionFit: Tart is a slang term for a promiscuous woman or prostitute.

clue.text: Film looks back to old city retrospectively

indicators.note: to means the next piece is attached to the previous one
retrospectively means looking backwards, so the word for old city is read in reverse

parts.note: the Great Wen is William Cobbett's old nickname for London

indicators.note: back means the word for looks is read the other way round

parts.note: leers are sly or lecherous looks

explanation.surface: A film that looks back nostalgically at an old city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Great Wen' is a nickname for London. 'back' turns LEERS into SREEL and 'retrospectively' turns WEN into NEW.
explanation.definitionFit: A short cinema film of current events, shown before features, is a type of film.

clue.text: Hold up basket

explanation.surface: Delaying a basket.
explanation.definitionFit: To hinder is to hold up or obstruct; a wicker container with a lid, as for picnics, is a basket.

clue.text: Be a satanist maybe with great energy

explanation.surface: Devil worship pursued with tremendous vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: A satanist might be fond of Satan himself; the idiom also means furiously or with tremendous vigour, as in 'ran like stink'.

clue.text: Cartoonist shows the man being given a thump by trendy boy

parts.note: he stands for the man
a throb is a beat or thump, as of the heart
in means fashionable or trendy
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A cartoonist depicting a man being punched by a fashionable youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thump' is a noun here, a heartbeat, not a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: W. Heath Robinson was a British illustrator famous for drawings of absurdly elaborate contraptions.

clue.text: At one villa I failed to offer relief

indicators.note: failed suggests the letters of at one villa I have broken down and been reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone at a holiday villa who failed to offer any help.
explanation.definitionFit: Easing of pain or distress is relief; the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Tramp in grass asleep

indicators.note: in means the word for tramp is placed inside the word for grass

parts.note: to grass is to inform on someone, as is to sing
to lumber is to tramp, walking heavily

explanation.surface: A vagrant sleeping in a meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tramp' reads as a vagrant but is a verb, walk heavily; 'grass' is the slang verb for informing.
explanation.definitionFit: Dozing and asleep are synonyms: both mean being in a state of rest.

clue.text: Deck sport returns around end of winter

indicators.note: around means the reversed sport goes round the picked letter
returns means the word for sport is read backwards

parts.note: polo is a sport played on horseback

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of the word winter

explanation.surface: Deck games resuming as winter draws to an end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns POLO into OLOP, and 'around' puts R from 'end of winter' inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: On old sailing ships the lowest deck was given this name.

clue.text: Drug satisfactorily obtained from plant

parts.note: speed is slang for amphetamine, a drug
well means satisfactorily

explanation.surface: A drug successfully extracted from a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Veronica, a small herb with blue flowers, is a plant.

clue.text: There's nothing to equal a romantic marriage

parts.note: love means nothing or zero in tennis scoring
to match is to equal

explanation.surface: A claim that nothing compares with marrying for love.
explanation.definitionFit: A union based on affection rather than money or status is a romantic marriage.

clue.text: Wild animal? Only Pussy, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the words are spoken and their sound gives the answer

parts.note: mere means only and a cat is a pussy

explanation.surface: Someone suggesting a supposed wild beast is just a pet cat.
explanation.definitionFit: This burrowing African mongoose is a wild creature, though not a cat, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Rumpus when manuscript full of rubbish is sent back

indicators.note: sent back means the whole assembly is reversed
full of means the word for rubbish fills the abbreviation for manuscript

parts.note: rot means rubbish or nonsense

explanation.surface: A fuss when a manuscript full of nonsense is returned to its author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' reverses the whole of MROTS, the manuscript filled with rubbish, not just the manuscript; 'Rumpus' is the definition, not a hint at chaos in the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An uproar or furious outburst is a rumpus.

clue.text: Is angry, possibly becoming lilac?

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of is angry may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone so angry they turn purple.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilac is the genus of shrubs whose botanical name it is.

clue.text: Warrior bishop who wrote poetically about Man?

parts.note: Alexander the Great was a famous warrior
the Pope is the Bishop of Rome

explanation.surface: A fighting churchman who wrote verse about mankind.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition alludes to 'An Essay on Man', a philosophical poem.
explanation.definitionFit: The eighteenth-century poet wrote 'An Essay on Man' in heroic couplets.

clue.text: Saint, to stomach unfermented grape juice

parts.note: tum is a childish word for stomach

explanation.surface: A holy man drinking unfermented grape juice.
explanation.definitionFit: Must, juice not yet turned into wine, is the old word's meaning.

clue.text: Attempt to arrest bumpkin not hard? Not that easy

indicators.note: arresting means holding, so the word for attempt holds the trimmed bumpkin

parts.note: a try is an attempt

indicators.note: not means the letter for hard is left out of the word for bumpkin

parts.note: a hick is a rustic bumpkin
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Trying to detain a soft country yokel is harder than it looks.
explanation.walkthrough: HICK loses H to leave ICK, which TRY holds.
explanation.definitionFit: Tricky and difficult are synonyms.

clue.text: For him, Trilby sang live, but unnaturally

definitions.text: For him, Trilby sang live, but unnaturally

indicators.note: unnaturally suggests the letters of sang live are put in an unnatural order

explanation.surface: Trilby performing live in a strange, entranced way for one man.
explanation.walkthrough: In George du Maurier's novel 'Trilby', the heroine sings only while hypnotised by this villain, so the whole clue describes him. 'unnaturally' rearranges SANGLIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: The sinister hypnotist in du Maurier's novel made the girl a singing star under his spell.

clue.text: Very eager not to finish earlier

indicators.note: not to finish means the last letter of the word for very eager is dropped

parts.note: agog means very eager

explanation.surface: Being too keen to complete something before its time.
explanation.definitionFit: Earlier and in the past are synonyms, as in 'two years before'.

clue.text: Tiny home to keep quiet about

indicators.note: about means the word for keep quiet goes round the word for home

parts.note: to mute is to silence or keep quiet
in means at home

explanation.surface: A small house where one must keep quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny and very small are synonyms.

clue.text: Everyone has a wish from the beginning

parts.note: all means everyone
to long is to wish or yearn

explanation.surface: Everybody has had one desire from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means throughout, the whole time since the start.
